Quick asks from our side to finalize the test matrix:

- Burst profiles: 500/1k/2k qps for 30s and 120s windows

Subject: Re: MAP benchmarking runs — preliminary results and logs

Team — ran the harness against staging-api.fastretail.com per matrix. Uploading full logs in burst_vs_steady_logs.tar.gz; summary below (high-level, raw numbers):

Burst runs (30s window)
- 500 qps: median TTFT 60ms, p95 token latency 180ms, no queue growth
- 1k qps: median TTFT 85ms, p95 260ms, queue occasional spikes up to 40 reqs at peak (30–35s into window)
- 2k qps: median TTFT 220ms, p95 540ms, observed sustained queue growth when sustained >45s; worker CPU saturated on one node

Steady-state (30 min runs)
- 100 qps: stable, p95 token latency 120ms, KV cache hit 68%
- 300 qps: stable, p95 token latency 230ms, KV cache hit 71%
- 600 qps: at ~18 minutes we saw queue depth grow; overall p95 420ms, intermittent 503s from the staging gateway when buffer exceeded threshold

TTFT (time-to-first-token) notes
- Short-turn requests (8–24 tokens) TTFT median 45–80ms depending on qps; TTFT degradation correlates with queue depth, not model execution time

Key observations and root causes
- Queueing is the dominant failure mode for bursts beyond 1k qps; the staging gateway’s default rate limiter is permissive and allows short large spikes that overflow worker pools
- Single-node CPU hotspots: some requests not well-balanced due to upstream connection pinning; need balancing and connection reuse tuning
- Prefix caching materially reduced token compute on repeated contexts — reuse improves throughput by ~12%

Recommendations (to include in MAP next steps)
1) Short-term (before procurement sign-off): enable leaky-bucket smoothing at gateway to cap per-second burst to sustained qps + small burst buffer (recommend smoothing window = 5s).
2) Mid-term: autoscale worker pool with faster provisioning for burst windows and tune connection pool to avoid pinning.
3) Rate-limit guidance for FastRetail: recommend published per-route soft limit of 1k qps with advertised fallback behavior; hard limit at 2k qps with 429 and graceful retries.
4) Acceptance criteria rewording: steady-state 300 qps p95 < 300ms; burst behavior: no unbounded queue growth within 2-minute sustained bursts at 1k qps.

I’ve attached the qps-latency-summary.png with charts; full traces in the tarball.

—Camila
Lead Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: burst_vs_steady_logs.tar.gz (logs, 42MB); qps-latency-summary.png (image, 180KB)
